column1: # The tracked paths that decide an Android release: the bytes of its system
# disk or the fields of its manifest. publish-release.py records the Git object
# ID of every `input` row (a tree for a directory, a blob for a file) in the
# release manifest, and the accepted descriptor repeats them. The release build
# of an application compares them with the commit it archives, so a change to an
# input that the accepted release does not carry stops the build
# A row covers its path and everything below it, and the longest row wins. An
# `excluded` row says why a path decides nothing; a tracked file that no row
# covers fails tests/tooling/android/test_release_inputs.py, so a new file is
# classified when it lands. Verifier-only tools, documentation and tests are
# excluded. The kernel is a separate artifact (kernel/*/artifacts), the release
# keeps its identity as provenance only, and no kernel path is listed.
